cells.tense: The work is underway and it has not turned on you.
cells.ask: Give one practice a set time this week, and let someone you trust see the work itself, not just the result.
cells.core:
You keep at this because it grows you, and it keeps giving back. The hours you put in return something steadier than they cost, so the time goes out without taking anything with it.

Quiet and alone is not hiding for you. It is where the attention goes, and what comes out of it is something you would stand behind rather than something you have to defend. The way you keep showing up is building a skill that is yours, not borrowed. You are getting to be more of what you already are, not proving anything to anyone. It could stand to be seen, and it would not go badly.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is steady, the life is wide, and it is still yours.
cells.verb: keeping a practice alive through repetition

cells.tense: You are running the same set again for a standard that keeps sliding.
cells.ask: Finish one practice and leave the work alone for a day, then hand someone a rough piece and hear what they see.
cells.core:
You can do more of this than most people, and the finish line keeps moving as you get close to it. The practice that was making you good is now mostly a way of staying ahead of something that will not be caught. The gap between what you did and what it could have been is what you are working on now.

Stopping has stopped feeling like a choice. Solitude that once fed the work now keeps the work out of sight, and the refining is less about the skill than about staying one step ahead of whatever would show up if you were not busy. The clearing comes when the shape falls, and some part of the day wants it to fall. Someone who knows the work could name the notch that is already enough — then you find out what is on the other side of putting it down.
cells.sheetLine: Practice has become proof, and the proof cannot be enough.

cells.tense: You once kept a practice going and something about it did not go well.
cells.ask: Pick one practice and do ten minutes today, no streak, no goal, and let it be small enough to lose.
cells.core:
You know the worth of steady practice. You have seen what it builds. Somewhere along the way it started feeling risky to keep, and you stepped back from it in a way you might not have said out loud. Cultivation takes time you are not sure you can spend, and there is a version of you that is doing fine without it. The wanting did not die. Nothing is wrong with wanting it; the door being closed is the issue.

What needs feeding is you in fair exchange, not a personal test. Start small enough that missing a day costs nothing, and let that be enough while something looser in you comes back. What you are cultivating is smaller than the fear you have of failing it. Begin where beginning costs almost nothing.

cells.tense: The skill is already arriving and you are still saying you just picked it up.
cells.ask: Name one thing you can do that took real hours, and write the sentence that says you did the hours.
cells.core:
You can do things that took time to build, and you have a way of talking about them as if they came easily. There are hours of work behind what you can do, and the explaining skips them, so the skill looks like luck. What is visible is the result. The repetition that made it is not on the record, and you are the one it belongs to.

You can already do what skill builds. What is missing is saying so, and that makes the ability feel less like yours than it is. Admitting the practice does not diminish the work; it hands your own hours back to you. You have been at this long enough.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is real. Say that it is yours.
